Completed runs record (NonCancellable), then refresh, then Added(pack.credits). In prod, OfflineFirstCreditsRepository.record only launches refresh() when remote.ownsLedger (OfflineFirstCreditsRepository.kt:55), so the client never credits; the server credits before RemotePaymentGateway returns Completed. Every RemotePaymentGateway path to PaymentUnconfirmed was traced: settleOwned miss, account generation change, server PURCHASE_INVALID/FORBIDDEN, and wallet generation stale. For each one, 'not confirmed yet' is true, and 'credits appear once confirmed' is conditional and therefore not false. findings.rule: 284-c10 / D68 ('N credits added' from the ledger delta); Constitution I.1 (copy must be true)
findings.trigger: Prod. The account has 3 credits on the server. The user opens the paywall while the network is down, so the init creditsRepository.refresh() fails silently and OfflineFirstCreditsRepository keeps held == null. observeBalance emits NO_SNAPSHOT 0 and the hero reads '0 credits left'. Back online, the user taps Restore purchases with nothing owned. before = observeBalance().first() = 0, restorePurchases() posts nothing, refresh() loads the real snapshot (3), and added = 3. The VM emits Added(3), so the toast says '3 credits added' and the route leaves the paywall (goBack, or replace with QuickQuestion). Nothing was restored. The same happens on a cold first visit if Restore is tapped before the init refresh lands: the restore's own refresh bumps the repository generation and discards the init result. The reverse also fails: if restorePurchases() credits a token but the following refresh() fails (it swallows errors), after == before and the user is told 'No previous purchases found'.
findings.title: Restore measures its delta against the unloaded placeholder balance, so it can claim credits were added when nothing was restored
findings.proof: PaywallViewModelTest: use a CreditsRepository fake modelled on OfflineFirstCreditsRepository. observeBalance emits 0 until the first successful refresh, the first refresh (init) throws or is swallowed, and later refreshes set 3. Use CountingPaymentGateway with nothing owned, call onRestore(), and assert events == [NothingToRestore]. Today it is [Added(3)].

findings.rule: Constitution I.1 (never state an untrue fact); 284-c1 'purchases with price'
findings.trigger: Prod. The user bought application_pack_15 on 5 Oct at ₹449. The owner later changes the Play price to ₹499, or Play shows a regional or promotional price. CreditsViewModel loads paymentGateway.packs(), so the history row reads 'Bought 15 credits / ₹499 · 5 Oct', a price the user never paid. The server ledger entry carries only productId and amount, and the price comes from today's ProductDetails. The plan chose this source, but the row reads as a receipt.
findings.title: History shows today's Play price as the price paid for past purchases

integrate_notes: Credits single source after #326 + #337 merge. #326 at 654f8469 moves SettingsViewModel to AccountCreditBalance.observeCredits() (PaymentGateway.observeEntitlement().totalCredits). The delete sheet already reads AccountCreditBalance through DeleteAccountUseCase.preview()/refreshedPreview(). This PR's Credits and Paywall read CreditsRepository.observeBalance(), and so does #277 JobResultViewModel (the paywall gate). After both merge, Settings and the delete sheet read the gateway, while Credits, Paywall and JobResult read the ledger repository. That contradicts D59(5) ('both read CreditsRepository after integration').

Prod effect: the numbers converge but can differ for a moment. apps-backend routes.ts serves /credits balance = wallet freeCredits + purchasedCredits, so both are the same server number. The client caches differ: WalletSource.cached refreshes on observeEntitlement onStart and after a purchase, and the OfflineFirstCreditsRepository snapshot refreshes on record/refresh. After a tailoring spend, the ledger refreshes (TailoringRunner record -> refresh) but the wallet cache does not until Settings re-subscribes. Before the first successful ledger fetch, Credits and Paywall show 0 while Settings can show the cached wallet count.

Demo effect: the numbers diverge permanently. OfflinePaymentGateway PaymentState starts with freeCredits = 1 and only unlock() spends (called only by OfflineSampleDataController). The Room ledger has no FREE_GRANT writer in main code and is debited by TailoringRunner SPEND rows. A new demo user sees Settings 1 and Credits/Paywall 0. After buying 15: Settings 16, Credits 15. After one tailoring: Settings 16, Credits 14. #277 JobResult in demo sends a new user to the paywall even though Settings says 1 credit.

Required at integration: pick one source for all four surfaces (Settings, delete sheet, Credits, Paywall) plus the JobResult gate, and record it as a decision that supersedes D59(5) or #326's change. Either point AccountCreditBalance.observeCredits/cachedCredits/unusedCredits at CreditsRepository (refresh first for unusedCredits), or point Credits, Paywall and JobResult at the gateway. Demo also needs the free grant and the spends in that one store. Add one app-level test that renders Settings, Credits and Paywall over the same fake state and asserts the same number, in demo and in prod.

Return-to-QuickQuestion after #277: QuickQuestionRoute on origin/revamp/277-job-analysis forwards to tailoring in a LaunchedEffect when the state is NoQuestion. So 'Buy' (or a Restore that emits Added) -> replace(QuickQuestion(app)) -> starts a tailoring run that spends a credit with no further tap. This matches the opener's own path (JobResult Tailor with credits -> QuickQuestion -> auto-forward), so it continues the original Tailor tap. Combined with the medium restore finding, though, a false 'credits added' can lead straight into a spend. The merge of #277 and #284 should include a wiring test that pins whichever behaviour is intended.

#280 (Application detail re-tailor) will be the second opener of PaywallNavKey(appId). If it opens the paywall from QuickQuestion itself rather than from a screen below it, replace() gives [.., QuickQuestion(app), QuickQuestion(app)]. Check the opener when #280 lands.
